calls.title: The welcome screen stays before the picks
calls.text: The concept opened on What do you want to do?; the build keeps the existing welcome first.
calls.what: Onboarding.tsx shows the lamp welcome as step 1, then groups, details and how it works.
calls.risk: One more Continue before the first choice.
calls.rec: Keep it: it is today's first impression and says nothing leaves this computer.
options: Start on What do you want to do?

calls.title: Pro is offered per pick, not as a grid for everyone
calls.text: The old Pro step listed eight Pro features to every new user. Now a picked Pro feature shows the price, Get Pro and Enter license key under it.
calls.what: GuideStep puts ProOffer under any Pro topic; the details step shows the license key box when a Pro feature is picked.
calls.risk: Someone who picks only free features never sees what Pro adds during setup. The Pro tab and the guide still show it.
calls.rec: Keep per pick: it answers what they asked for and stays quiet otherwise.
options: Add one line on Pro to the groups step

calls.title: A pick this platform lacks still shows (done)
calls.text: Today every Pro feature runs on macOS, Windows and Linux, so no pick is missing. A future feature that skips a platform would have vanished from Your picks.
calls.what: Done (f0e44b660): such a pick now shows with the line Coming to this computer soon, plus Get Pro.
calls.risk: None today; this guards the next feature that ships on fewer platforms.

calls.title: One video player for guide clips
calls.text: Desktop has the chat preview player in core and Video Studio's fuller player in Pro. The guide is core.
calls.what: Guide clips (step 15) need play, scrub, speed and full screen.
calls.risk: Two players drift; the guide cannot use the Pro one.
calls.rec: Move the fuller player into core; Video Studio, chat and the guide all use it.
calls.recommended: Move the full player to core
options: Move the full player to core
Guide uses the chat preview as it is

calls.title: Where voice-over audio lives
calls.text: Tour voice-overs are made on this Mac with Kokoro.
calls.what: The narration text and its hash live in shared; the audio files are generated into each app's assets.
calls.risk: A shared copy of audio loads differently in Vite and Metro: a build risk for little gain.
calls.rec: Same files written into each app; text and hash stay in shared.
options: One copy in the shared package

calls.title: Voice-over voice and languages
calls.text: You chose all 12 app languages in one release.
calls.what: Tours speak in one Kokoro voice.
calls.risk: Audio in 12 languages is 12 times the files and checks; English-only audio in a German app feels half done.
calls.rec: One English voice you pick from 3 samples, with the captions translated in all 12 languages.

calls.title: Where the extension's first run starts
calls.text: Today nothing opens on install; the side panel opens on Settings with Pair with desktop.
calls.what: background/shortcuts.ts listens to onInstalled only to build the right-click menu. Panel.tsx shows SettingsScreen setupOnly when not paired.
calls.risk: A new person sees a pairing button with no idea what the extension does or that it needs the computer app with Pro.
calls.rec: Open a welcome tab once on install (never on update). The side panel cannot open itself without a click, so a tab is the only place a first run can start. It ends with Open the side panel.

calls.title: Picks first, then connect
calls.text: Desktop and mobile ask what you want, then which ones, then how it works. The extension also needs to connect to your computer.
calls.what: Pairing (PairingCard) already has every state: found, waiting for the six words, declined, no Pro, not found.
calls.risk: Connect first puts a technical step before any value. Picks first could ask for things the computer then lacks.
calls.rec: Picks first, the same as every app, then Connect. After pairing, add the picks made on the computer that run in the browser, marked From your computer.
options: Connect first, start from the computer's picks

calls.title: The extension says Free where it needs Pro
calls.text: features.json marks Chat, Ask about a photo, Images, Web Use and Web search Free, and the extension uses those tiers. But the extension works only with Desktop Pro.
calls.what: panel-gate.ts opens chat only when the desktop reports features.pro; otherwise it shows the Pro or setup screen. features.json parts have tier 'free' with no extension override.
calls.risk: A person picks five Free things, then meets a Pro wall at Connect.
calls.rec: Tell the truth now: mark every extension part Pro in features.json (a per-platform tier, as Dictation already has). Making the free parts work without Pro is a separate product change.
options: Make free parts work without Pro

calls.title: Ask for site access once, by pick
calls.text: Site access is asked in three places at first use: useSiteAccess, BrowserTasksRow and SettingsScreen.
calls.what: Each calls browser.permissions.request on its own, with its own words.
calls.risk: Scribe or Passwords seem broken until a prompt appears somewhere else.
calls.rec: One step in the first run lists only what the picks need, one line each with why, each skippable. The three places call the same owner later.
calls.recommended: Ask once in the first run
options: Ask once in the first run

calls.title: No way to get the computer app
calls.text: With no desktop found, the panel says Start Off Grid AI Desktop and shows 127.0.0.1:7878.
calls.what: DesktopOffline.tsx shows the address and a retry, with no download link.
calls.risk: A person who installed the extension first is stuck.
calls.rec: Get Off Grid AI for your computer (download page) and I have it, look again. The address moves under Settings.
